title: Total interest on a loan
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No existing point covers total interest as total repayments minus the amount borrowed, or how the loan term affects it; reducing balance loans and compound interest are related but teach different ideas.

draft.title: Total interest on a loan
card: The total paid on a loan = repayment × number of repayments. Total interest = total paid − amount borrowed.
Example: Sam borrows $10 000 and repays $450 a month for 24 months. Total paid = 450 × 24 = $10 800. Total interest = 10 800 − 10 000 = $800.
A longer term makes each repayment smaller, because the loan is spread over more payments.
A longer term also means interest is charged for more time, so the total interest is usually much larger.
draft.remember: Total interest = total paid − amount borrowed. A longer term means smaller repayments but more interest.

a.q: Priya borrows $8000 and repays $250 a month for 36 months. What is the total interest?
a.why: Total paid = 250 × 36 = $9000. Total interest = 9000 − 8000 = $1000. The $9000 is the total paid, not the interest, because the amount borrowed has not yet been taken off.
a.clue: Find the total paid first, then take off the amount borrowed.

b.q: Tom borrows $20 000. Plan A: $620 a month for 36 months. Plan B: $390 a month for 60 months. Which statement is correct?
opts: Plan B has $1080 more interest than Plan A
Plan A has $1080 more interest than Plan B
Plan B has $3400 more interest than Plan A
Plan A and Plan B have the same total interest
b.why: Plan A total = 620 × 36 = $22 320, so interest is $2320. Plan B total = 390 × 60 = $23 400, so interest is $3400. Plan B costs $1080 more in interest, even though its repayments are smaller.
b.clue: Work out the interest for each plan, then compare them.

b.best: Plan B has $1080 more interest than Plan A

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out ($1000; Plan B interest $3400 versus Plan A $2320, a $1080 difference), and the card and explanations are accurate.
